title: Manager EDI
description:
Hi, weâre Gravie. Our mission is to create health benefits that actually benefit small and midsize businesses and their employees. Our innovative benefit solutions and services are developed and delivered by a diverse group of unique people. We encourage you to be your authentic self - we like you that way.

A Little More About The Role:

Weâre looking for an Manager, EDI to own how Gravie exchanges eligibility, enrollment, and claims data with our partners and internal systems as our book of level-funded health plans grows. This leader will report to the Director of Configuration and will build and lead a team that configures, tests,and monitors these connections, while setting the standards that keep them accurate, secure, and scalable.. This role carries meaningful latitude to shape process, tooling, and team structure, and is expected to represent EDI in cross-functional forums.

You Will:

â Lead, develop, and scale a team of EDI analysts, including hiring, mentoring, performance management, and cross-training so no process depends on one person.

â Own the EDI program, including standards for file specifications, mapping, naming, scheduling, and documentation, and maintain an inventory of every trading partner, file, and schedule with a clear owner for each.

â Manage new trading partner setup from requirements through UAT and go-live, translating business needs from Product, Enrollment, Operations, and Finance into clear technical specifications.

â Oversee daily monitoring of inbound and outbound X12 transactions (834, 837, 835, 278, and acknowledgments such as 999, TA1, and 277CA), and drive failures and rejects to root cause.

â Establish error handling, alerting, reconciliation, and QA standards so issues are caught before members, providers, or groups are affected.

â Own EDI trading partner, clearinghouse, and vendor relationships, including SLA performance and escalation resolution.

â Manage off-cycle changes, renewals, and system upgrades without disrupting daily processing, and lead cross-functional planning for open enrollment and Q4.

â Ensure all data exchange follows HIPAA, privacy, and security requirements, including secure transfer (SFTP and encryption), and partner with Security and Compliance on reviews and audits.

â Help shape and drive the automation roadmap, evaluating tools and approaches (including APIs and connectivity platforms) that deliver measurable efficiency and quality improvements.

â Build runbooks, documentation, and compliance practices that hold up under audit.

â Provide visibility to leadership on volumes, error rates, turnaround times, risk, and capacity across EDI.

â Act as the primary escalation point for complex, high-stakes EDI issues, exercising independent judgment to resolve risk before it reaches leadership.

â Demonstrate commitment to our core competencies of being authentic, curious, creative, empathetic, and outcome oriented.

You Bring:

â 7+ years of healthcare EDI experience, including 2+ years leading a team in EDI, configuration, claims operations, or healthcare IT.

â Deep working knowledge of HIPAA X12 transaction standards (834, 837, 835, 278) and acknowledgments, and how they integrate with enrollment, claims configuration, and adjudication.

â Hands-on experience with file validation, mapping, and troubleshooting, including reading raw X12 and identifying loop and segment issues.

â Experience in benefits administration, enrollment and eligibility, or claims processing, ideally in a TPA, payer, or carrier environment.

â Experience managing trading partner onboarding, testing, and UAT, and working with clearinghouses or vendors against defined SLAs

â Working knowledge of SFTP and secure file transfer practices.

â Strong communication and cross-functional relationship-building skills, with the ability to explain technical issues to non-technical stakeholders.

â Ability to operate strategically while remaining close enough to the details to guide the team through complex technical problems.

â Ability to deal with ambiguity, shift gears comfortably, and take decisive action without having the total picture.

â Strong organizational, time management, and prioritization skills, with the judgment to know what needs leadership visibility versus what the team should own.

Extra credit:

â Experience with EDI and integration tools

â SQL skills for data validation and reconciliation.

â Familiarity with API-based integrations, FHIR, or 270/271 transactions.

â Experience supporting system integrations or large-scale platform migrations.

â Previous experience in a startup or high-growth company environment.

A Little More About Us:

  • We know healthcare. Our company was founded and is still led by industry veterans who have started and grown several market-leading companies in the space.

  • We have raised money from top tier investors who share the same long-term vision as we do of building an industry defining company that will endure over the long run. We are well capitalized.

  • Our clients love us. Customer satisfaction rates among employees using Gravie health plans consistently rank above 80% â nearly 40 points above the industry average.

  • Our culture is unique. We tend to be non-hierarchical, merit-driven, opinionated but kind people who thrive working in a high-performance, fast-paced environment. People at Gravie care deeply about making a positive impact in the lives of the people we serve.

Benefits

Our unique benefits program is the gravy, i.e., the special sauce that sets our compensation package apart. In addition to standard health and wellness benefits, Gravieâs package includes alternative medicine coverage, flexible PTO, up to 16 weeks paid parental leave, paid holidays, a 401k program, transportation perks, education reimbursement, and 2 days of paid paw-ternity leave.

Job Applicants

If you apply for employment with Gravie, personal information collected via our applicant tracking vendor is subject to our standalone California Job Applicant Notice at Collection, accessible directly within the application workflow and separate from this Policy.

title: Legal Engineering Counsel
description:
We're building a new healthcare clearinghouse

Stedi is the only headless clearinghouse and RCM engine. Headless means every part of our product is accessible via API. Developers and AI agents build their own interface on top of it. By offering modern, AI-ready APIs alongside traditional real-time and batch EDI processes, we enable both healthcare technology businesses and established players to exchange mission-critical transactions. Our clearinghouse product and customer-first approach have set us apart. Stedi was ranked by Ramp as one of the fastest-growing SaaS vendors.

Stedi has lightning in a bottle: engineers and designers shipping products week in and week out; a lean business team supporting the company's infrastructure; a passion for automation and eliminating toil; and $142 million in funding from top investors like Stripe, Addition, USV, Bloomberg Beta, First Round Capital, and more.

To see what we ship, watch the 2026 Stedi Keynote. To learn more about how we work, watch our founder Zack's interview with First Round Capital.

What weâre looking for

Stedi is hiring a Legal Engineering Counsel to build how our legal work gets done, and to own a large share of it. Every new customer, payer connection, and partnership runs through a contract, and the volume grows every month. Youâll design the systems that handle it (playbooks, review workflows, automation, and AI tooling) and run them on live deals with counterparties ranging from fast-moving healthtech startups to national payers.

This role pairs legal practice with technical skill. You bring strong legal training and a feel for how commercial deals work, and youâve used AI and other technology to make legal work faster and more consistent. What you learn on live deals shapes the systems, and better systems make the next deal faster.

Youâll join a small, effective Legal team with a broad mandate. We keep up with a fast-growing, highly regulated business by investing in good systems and tools, and this role sits at the center of that investment. Healthcare experience is not required â we value strong judgment, curiosity, and the ability to learn a new industry quickly. If you have the talent and drive to help build a world-class legal function alongside Stediâs experienced legal counsel mentors at a rapidly scaling tech company, we want to talk.

What youâll do

  • Build and own the systems behind Stediâs contracting, including playbooks, clause libraries, templates, intake and approval workflows, and AI-assisted first-pass review.

  • Break recurring legal work into repeatable steps with clear inputs, decision points, and escalation paths, then decide what to automate, what to standardize, and what needs a lawyer.

  • Turn our legal counselâs nuanced advice, negotiation positions, and fallbacks into structured guidance that people and AI tools can apply consistently.

  • Test and measure what you build. Check outputs against real deals, track where the tools fall short, and iterate until they hold up.

  • Draft and negotiate contracts yourself using those systems â including customer agreements, BAAs, NDAs, payer trading partner agreements â from first redline through signature.

  • Structure our contract data so the team (and our tools) can answer questions about our agreements in minutes.

  • Partner with Sales and Account Management. Build self-serve paths for routine agreements and field the questions that still need a person.

  • Take on new areas based on interest and business need as Stedi and the Legal team grow.

Who you are

  • Youâre bar-admitted and want to practice law while building the systems that support it.

  • BigLaw or in-house experience, ideally on transactional work, is a strong plus.

  • Youâve built with technology, whether thatâs AI workflows, prompts and evaluations, automations, scripts, or no-code tools, and you can show what you made.

  • Youâre comfortable working with structured data and technical tools, and you pick up new ones quickly. Coding experience is a plus, not a requirement.

  • You can explain complex issues in plain language, write clearly, and communicate confidently with executives, lawyers, procurement staff, engineers, and everyone in between.

  • Youâre comfortable with high-volume work, ambiguity, and shifting priorities, and you maintain high quality through effective habits.

  • You move fast, operate with precision, and follow through until the job is done. You thrive in an environment where clarity, accountability, and urgency matter. Youâre hungry to learn, seek out feedback, and put it to work.

Weâve been made aware of individuals impersonating the Stedi recruiting team. Please note:

  • All official communication about roles at Stedi will only come from an @stedi.com email address, or from our official identification verification partner, Persona, @frompersona.com.

  • If youâre unsure whether a message is legitimate or have any concerns, feel free to contact us directly at careers@stedi.com.

We appreciate your attention to this and your interest in joining Stedi.

At Stedi, we're looking for people who are deeply curious and aligned to our ways of working. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't perfectly match the job description.
